hecatomb: a great public sacrifice of many animals to the gods
rosy-fingered: Homeric epithet describing the dawn as glowing pink
sea-girt: surrounded or encircled by the sea
grey-eyed: epithet describing the goddess Athena with grey eyes
hapless: unlucky, unfortunate, without any good fortune
redoubtable: formidable and inspiring fear or respect in others
lordly: proud and haughty, like a lord or nobleman
insolence: rude, arrogant behaviour showing contempt for others
mettle: courage, spirit, and determination in facing difficulty
havoc: widespread destruction and confusion, causing great damage
mischief: trouble, harm, or annoying behaviour caused by someone
propitiate: appease or win favour of a god or person
vouchsafe: grant or give condescendingly, as a favour
ordained: decreed or determined by fate or a higher power
bethought: remembered or called to mind, reflected upon
spake: old-fashioned past tense of speak, meaning spoke
marvelled: wondered with amazement at something surprising
brooding: sitting in gloomy, anxious, or resentful thought
counselled: advised or gave guidance to someone
rejoinder: a quick reply, especially a sharp answer to criticism
contentions: disputes or quarrels between people or groups
wedded: married, joined in marriage to another person
wooing: courting someone in order to win their love
suitors: men seeking to win a woman's hand in marriage
asunder: into separate pieces, apart from one another
avenge: take revenge on someone for a wrong done
avenged: took revenge for a wrong done to someone
hence: from this place or time; for this reason
thence: from that place; for that reason
henceforward: from this time onward into the future
to-morrow: the day after today, archaic spelling
abode: a dwelling place or home where someone lives
cloisters: covered walkways around an inner courtyard in a building
handmaids: female servants or attendants in a household
housekeeper: a servant who manages the running of a household
barrow: a burial mound raised over a grave
chariot: a two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses, used in war
steeds: horses, especially spirited or noble ones
yoked: harnessed to a cart or plough, joined to pull together
heifer: a young cow that has not yet had a calf
paunch: the stomach or belly of an animal
spits: long metal rods on which meat is skewered and roasted
mixing-bowls: large bowls in which wine was mixed with water
fleet: a group of ships sailing together under one command
headland: a high point of land jutting out into the sea
inward: toward the inside or interior of a place
meats: food in general, especially cooked flesh of animals
spunging: living at others' expense, sponging off their generosity
disposed: inclined or willing to do something
false-minded: deceitful, treacherous, or untrustworthy in thought and intent
stranger: a guest or foreigner, someone from another land
sprinkling: scattering small drops of liquid, often as an offering
